We often discuss tool use as a single capability. In reality, it is a sequence of five distinct mechanical steps and the failure of any one of them halts the entire process. First, the model must detect the need for a tool and pause its internal generation. Then, it has to scan a catalog and select the specific tool required for the task. The most common point of failure is argument filling. If the AI produces a slight formatting error in the parameters, like a three-letter airport code where the system expects a full city name, the input is rejected and the sequence crashes. If the arguments are correct, the system must then safely execute the action and integrate the resulting raw data back into the AI's reasoning loop. Because these nodes are linked, an error at step two or step four results in the same outcome, total operational collapse. Making these actions work in production requires a dedicated execution layer. This layer ensures all actions run in sandboxed leastprivilege environments to prevent a single logic error from executing unintended commands on the main system. And then there is the observation layer. If a tool fails and returns a 5,000line raw JSON error, feeding that directly back into the AI creates context pollution, overwhelming its ability to reason. The observation layer filters this chaos, translating a raw data dump into a clean, typed summary that keeps the AI focused on the next logical step.
